prod_vs_preprod.summary: Preprod's BLOCKED verdict reproduces exactly on production. Eleven exact-match invocations (name/identifier/id, individually) against three independent production folders on project 332537 — folder 9697326 'MCP Testing' (3 cases, using TC-838571/TC-838570/TC-838569), folder 40231630 'Automation' (~972-1168 cases, using TC-6268089), and folder 7772651 'prd' (16 cases, using TC-1041802) — all real, freshly-confirmed-existing cases (confirmed via search_project_entities_v2 immediately beforehand) all returned HTTP 200 with body []. This is not a small-sample or single-folder fluke: production has 16,267 cases across 294 folders, and even the 972-case folder produced zero rows for an exact id/identifier/name match on a case proven to exist in it seconds earlier. This directly corroborates the capability's own guidance text verbatim ('DEPRECATED AND EFFECTIVELY DEAD... queries the legacy local test-case table, which is no longer the system of record... returns an empty list with 200, whatever you search for') using abundant real production data, ruling out the preprod-data-starvation hypothesis.

notes: Because no invocation of search_test_cases_by_folder_v1 ever returned a non-empty array (on either preprod or prod), item shape (test_case_steps type, sibling steps field, count/info agreement) could not be inspected on prod either — there is no successful non-empty response to examine. This is expected and consistent with the capability being genuinely dead rather than a payload error: all calls were exact-match on name/identifier/id fields exactly as declared, all against cases independently confirmed to exist via search_project_entities_v2 moments before each attempt, across three folders spanning 3 to ~1168 cases. Verdict is BLOCKED (matching preprod) rather than PASS, because a 200 on an empty collection is only unremarkable when the queried data genuinely has no matches — here the whole point of the probe was to determine whether emptiness reflects real absence or dead-capability behavior, and prod's abundant real data with zero hits settles it as the latter. DRIFT was ruled out because prod did NOT contradict preprod's dead-capability framing — it corroborated it with much stronger evidence (larger dataset, three folders, freshly-verified real data) than preprod could produce.
